# The PlatformIO platform's own virtualenv (penv) for the firmware release
# build, every package pinned with its SHA-256. The release workflow creates
# ~/.platformio/penv with these before `pio run`, installed with
# `pip install --require-hashes --no-deps --only-binary=:all:`, then builds
# with UV_OFFLINE=1 and UV_NO_BUILD_ISOLATION=1: the platform's
# builder/penv_setup.py finds every dependency it wants already installed,
# installs esptool editable from the checked tool-esptoolpy package with the
# setuptools pinned here, and cannot fetch anything else from PyPI.
# scripts/pin_firmware_toolchain.py refuses a platform whose penv_setup.py
# wants a package this file lacks (prepare) and a penv holding anything not
# pinned here (check). esptool is left out: it comes from tool-esptoolpy.
# Python 3.12 on linux x86_64 (the workflow's runner). Regenerate with
#   uv pip compile firmware/requirements-penv.in \
#     --override firmware/requirements-penv.overrides.txt \
#     --python-version 3.12 --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28 \
#     --generate-hashes --only-binary :all: --no-header \
#     -o firmware/requirements-penv.txt
# and put this header back.
# Known advisories, accepted because this environment exists only on the
# ephemeral release runner and serves no network: starlette (capped below 1.0
# by pioarduino's `starlette<1`; it serves PIO Home, which `pio run` never
# starts) and ecdsa (no fixed release; esptool's secure-boot signing, which
# the release build does not call). Dependabot alerts on this file are
# expected; dismiss them as build-only ("vulnerable code is not used") and
# revisit when pioarduino lifts the starlette cap.
